Done. Committed as `dadee0e` on `hive/SCRUM-5`; working tree is clean, nothing pushed.

## Summary

- **CONTRIBUTING.md** — added a "Build and test locally" section between "Dev setup" and "Before every commit". It shows `go build ./...`, building and running the CLI from `./cmd/hivedispatch`, `go test -race ./...`, and how to run a single test in one package. A one-line note explains the suite is hermetic (fakes under `internal/`, no credentials or network needed).
- **README.md** — the "Design" section now links to [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) alongside the existing design-spec and decisions links, using the same link style.

Verification: `go build ./...` succeeds, `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test -race ./...` passes with zero failures. No code changes were made.

This asks for a new ticket-tracking/claim backend, not a small feature addition. Today GitHub is only used as a `githost.GitHost` (internal/githost/github/github.go) to find/open PRs via the REST API — there is no GitHub Issues tracker in this repo, and the ticket's premise ("GitHub works now with labels on issues") doesn't match the codebase. All queue, claim, and state semantics are Jira-only by explicit design (docs/design-spec.md: "Jira owns the queue and the claims... the single most important decision in the spec"), implemented via internal/tracker/jira against the Tracker interface (internal/tracker/tracker.go). "Moving tickets across a GitHub Projects board" would require: a new GraphQL-based client for Projects v2 (REST doesn't support it), a way to represent/claim tickets and move them between status columns, and either a second Tracker implementation or a redesign of the Jira-owns-claims invariant the whole claim protocol depends on. That's a cross-cutting architectural change spanning tracker, dispatch, and config, not something one PR can land safely, and it runs counter to a deliberate design decision rather than extending it.

Done. Two commits on `hive/SCRUM-5`, working tree clean, nothing pushed. `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` (0 failures), and `golangci-lint run ./...` (0 issues) all pass module-wide.

## Summary

**What changed**

- **`internal/config`** — new optional `github.project` block: `owner`, `number` (from the board URL), `field` (default `Status`), and `columns` (one option name per state, defaulting to `Ready` / `In Progress` / `Needs Info` / `In Review` / `Needs Human`). `Enabled()` is false when the block is absent; when present, owner and number are validated with hints pointing at the URL.
- **`internal/tracker/ghissues/project.go`** (new) — GraphQL client for Projects v2, posted to `graphql` resolved against `api_url` (so GHES lands on `/api/graphql`). Resolves the board once via `repositoryOwner(login:) { ... on ProjectV2Owner { projectV2 } }` (works for users and orgs without an owner-type setting), caches it, and re-reads once if a column is missing so a column added while the worker runs is picked up. `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPES` errors tell the user `gh auth refresh -s project`.
- **`Transition`** — after the label swap, when a board is configured: finds the issue's existing item on that board (via the REST `node_id`), adds it with `addProjectV2ItemById` if missing, then sets the option with `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue`. A board failure returns an error naming the label that did land; the dispatcher already logs transition errors rather than failing the run, so labels stay authoritative and the board is a mirror.
- **`Check` / `check -live`** — resolves the board and reports its title, missing columns, or why it was unreachable; any of those fails `OK()`.
- **Docs** — starter config comment block, a "A GitHub Projects board" subsection in `docs/setup.md` (including the extra `project` token scope), and a `docs/decisions.md` entry recording the mirror-not-owner decision and the alternatives rejected (polling the board, rolling back labels, auto-creating options).

**Tests** — config defaults/validation; tracker tests using a fake `/graphql` handler covering add-then-move, no second add on the next transition, no GraphQL calls at all without the block, missing-column refresh, scope-error hint, and `Check` reporting for found/missing-columns/unreachable boards.

**Not done / to note** — columns are not created automatically (GitHub's `updateProjectV2Field` replaces the whole option list, so it's left to the user; `check -live` says exactly which are missing). For your board at `github.com/users/thomasmeadows/projects/2`, the config is `github.project.owner: thomasmeadows`, `number: 2`, plus column names matching your board — and the token needs the `project` scope, which the default `gh auth login` token does not include.
